subject: Production distress: 5xx/429 avalanche during peak inference window
messages:
From: Jennifer Park <jennifer.park@apexhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Cc: ops@apexhealth.com, Mike Chen <mike.chen@apexhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 14:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: production anomalies - increased 5xx/429 rates

Hi Marissa,

We just started our morning peak and are seeing a sharp spike of 5xx and 429 responses from Redwood for the /v1/generate endpoint. Latency for successful requests has also jumped from ~120ms to 2-3s for many calls. Our ingestion service is retrying aggressively and we are now seeing request pile-up and some timeouts upstream.

Sample: attached CSV has a 10-minute window of request ids and status codes. The error rate went from ~0.3% to ~18% at 13:55 UTC and hasn’t fully recovered. This is impacting clinical routing and we’ve had several customer-facing errors already.

Can you escalate? We need an ETA for mitigation and any recommended temporary client-side knobs (backoff, concurrency) while you investigate.

Thanks,
Jennifer
Sr Product Ops, ApexHealth

Attachments: ApexHealth-error-sample.csv (CSV, 14KB)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: Jennifer Park <jennifer.park@apexhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 14:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: production anomalies - increased 5xx/429 rates

Jennifer — thanks for the flag and the sample. I’m putting together a rapid response:

1) War room: joining now (Rishi + Laura + infra oncall).
2) Immediate ask for you: could you reduce retries to max 2 attempts with exponential backoff and lower concurrency by 30% if possible. That will limit the effect of a retry storm while we triage.
3) We’ll push a temporary routing change if we confirm pool exhaustion.

Rishi — can you confirm if this looks like a Dedicated GPU pool saturation / autoscale lag or something else? Laura, I’ll need exec support if we have to authorize burst capacity or credits.

I’ll update Jen within 15 minutes with the first observations.

—Marissa

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com

Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 14:25:00 +0000
Subject: Re: production anomalies - initial triage notes (ApexHealth)

Marissa / team — quick triage summary (first 20 min):

- Observed behavior: sudden spike in 5xx and 429 originating from the us-west-2 Dedicated pool serving ApexHealth tenant. Metrics show connection failures -> 5xx (worker unavailable) and 429s from the request router returning "queue full".
- Root cause hypothesis: GPU capacity exhaustion in the dedicated fleet combined with the autoscaler under-reacting to the sharp ramp (scale-up O(90s) under current policy). The client retry pattern created a feedback loop causing a retry amplification.
- Evidence: attached graphs (gpu-pool-metrics-20280309.png) show GPU utilization hitting 99% across the pool at 13:53 UTC and node churn shortly after. Agent logs show autoscaler decisions delayed due to threshold hysteresis.

Immediate mitigations enacted (14:22–14:24 UTC):
- Temporarily injected a policy override to allow burst nodes in the dedicated fleet (+4 nodes) — reduced queue lengths but initial kube pod warmup delayed KV cache warming for hot keys.
- Enabled a fast-fallback route to the smaller, lower-cost variant (quantized model) for non-critical endpoints for this customer to reduce per-request GPU time.
- Bumped client-side rate-limiting recommendations to Jen (see Marissa’s note).

Short-term next steps (next 2 hours):
- Tune autoscaler hysteresis and scale aggressiveness for this pool (JIRA-987 created).
- Add temporary request shaping on the edge to prevent retries escalating (throttle by IP/tenant).
- Postmortem to identify why the scale-up did not provision fast enough (likely kube eviction + warm caching).

Longer-term: investigate warm standby nodes and prefix KV cache prewarming for hot tenants, plus revisit default autoscale profiles for Dedicated pools with bursty arrival patterns.

Attachments: gpu-pool-metrics-20280309.png, triage-traces-20280309.zip

—Rishi
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: production anomalies - update and temporary mitigations

Jennifer — quick update and action plan: thanks for the error sample. Our engineering lead (Rishi) confirmed pool exhaustion + autoscale lag. We executed the following immediate mitigations:

- Burst capacity enabled (+4 nodes) and fallback routing to a quantized model for non-critical calls — you should see error rate drop.
- Please apply: set client retries to max 2 with exponential backoff and reduce concurrency by ~30% for the next 60 minutes.
- We are also applying tenant-level request shaping to slow retry amplification.

Estimated timeline: we expect to see error rate fall within 10–20 minutes of these mitigations as pods come up and cache warms. If there’s no improvement within 30 minutes we’ll open a formal incident and route to exec leadership (Laura & Evelyn).

I’ll keep you posted every 15 minutes. Sorry for the disruption — we’ll follow up with an incident report and action items.

Best,
Marissa

Summary:
- Impact: ApexHealth (large clinical customer, high SLA tier) experienced a 5xx/429 spike at ~13:53 UTC during peak traffic caused by Dedicated GPU pool exhaustion and autoscaling lag. Error rate peaked ~18% for 10–12 minutes.
- Mitigation: Burst nodes + quantized fallback + tenant shaping applied; metrics show error rate falling to ~1.5% after mitigations.

Immediate asks of leadership:
1) Approve one-time burst capacity billing override / credit for ApexHealth for the incident window (we may have to absorb some cost at scale).
2) Approve priority postmortem and engineering task force to implement warm-standby/prewarm KV cache and revision of autoscale profiles for Dedicated pools.

Next steps: Rishi will prepare a technical postmortem (JIRA-987) and timeline for fixes; Marissa will coordinate customer comms and remediation credits. We should schedule a 30-min readout with the customer and product within 48 hours.

—Laura
